headline: Not yet: hot inflation and Nvidia scandal keep pressure at 69
summary: Stocks slipped on Tuesday 10 November (S&P 500 −0.38%, Nasdaq −0.74%) as hot October CPI lifted Fed hike odds and Nvidia fell 5.5%. The basket scores 68.4; pressure holds at 69. [1][22]

signals.label: Shiller CAPE
signals.eli5: Share prices divided by ten years of average company profits, so one good or bad year cannot fool it. The higher it is, the more people are paying for each dollar of profit.

signals.label: Chips ÷ S&P 500 (SOX ratio)
signals.eli5: The main chip-maker index compared with the S&P 500. Chips are the picks and shovels of the AI boom, so this shows how much of the market's bet is riding on it.

signals.label: 10-year Treasury yield
signals.eli5: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years. When it rises, safe bonds compete with shares, and expensive stocks are the first to look less attractive.

signals.label: S&P 500 price to sales
signals.note: beyond any prior burst; basket score 100
signals.eli5: The value of the 500 biggest US companies divided by their sales. Sales are harder to dress up than profits, so a high ratio says prices have run far ahead of what firms sell.

analysis: The basket scores 68.4: fragility 80.6, trigger 32.1, confirmation 88.0. Price to sales (3.71), household equities (48.2% of financial assets) and subprime auto delinquency (5.98%) sit beyond any prior burst; CAPE is 39.70 and unemployment (4.1%) scores 93.3. The BIS credit gap, at −11.3 points, is the calmest reading. [3][7][13][2][12][9]

On Tuesday 10 November the S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,520.93 and the Nasdaq 0.74%, as hotter-than-expected October inflation raised bets on a December Fed hike. Nvidia dropped 5.5% to $168.80 on reports tied to CEO Jensen Huang and a board probe; AMD and Broadcom rallied. Earnings are due 17 November. [1][22]

The 10-year yield rose to 4.98% on 10 November and the high-yield spread was 334 bp on 9 November, so credit stress is modest. Anthropic's IPO is set to price on 18 November at up to a $1.405 trillion valuation, a test for the AI trade. Why 69: the basket anchors near 68 and news adds +1. [11][8][23]

indicators.label: Shiller CAPE, S&P 500
indicators.detail: S&P 500 cyclically adjusted P/E, multpl.com monthly table
indicators.eli5: Share prices divided by ten years of average company profits, so one good or bad year cannot fool it. The higher it is, the more people are paying for each dollar of profit.

indicators.label: S&P 500 price to sales
indicators.detail: Price over trailing 12-month sales, multpl.com; beyond any burst
indicators.eli5: The value of the 500 biggest US companies divided by their sales. Sales are harder to dress up than profits, so a high ratio says prices have run far ahead of what firms sell.

indicators.label: Nasdaq Composite ÷ S&P 500
indicators.detail: Nasdaq Composite ÷ S&P 500 close, Yahoo chart data
indicators.eli5: How the tech-heavy Nasdaq compares with the broader S&P 500. When this climbs, money is piling into tech faster than into everything else, which is what past bubbles looked like.

indicators.label: Margin debt growth, year on year
indicators.detail: FINRA margin debit balances, Aug 2026 vs Aug 2025
indicators.eli5: How much more money investors have borrowed from their brokers to buy shares than a year ago. Borrowed bets pile up in a boom and get sold in a hurry when prices fall.

indicators.label: Household equities as share of assets
indicators.detail: Fed Z.1 via FRED, Q2 2026; beyond any prior burst
indicators.eli5: The slice of ordinary households' savings that sits in shares. The bigger the slice, the fewer new buyers are left to push prices up, and the harder a fall would hit.

indicators.label: US high-yield bond spread
indicators.detail: ICE BofA US high-yield OAS in bp, FRED
indicators.eli5: The extra interest risky companies pay to borrow compared with the US government. A small gap means lenders are relaxed; a widening gap often comes just before trouble.

indicators.label: BIS credit-to-GDP gap, US
indicators.detail: Private credit to GDP minus its trend, BIS, Q1 2026
indicators.eli5: How far total US borrowing has run ahead of its usual path relative to the size of the economy. Near zero is routine; a big positive gap has come before most credit busts.

indicators.label: Fed funds target, 12-month change
indicators.detail: Upper bound 4.00% vs 4.25% a year earlier (−25bp), FRED
indicators.eli5: How much the Fed has raised its main interest rate over the past year. Higher rates make borrowing dearer and have pricked past bubbles; a year of cuts counts as zero here.

indicators.label: 10-year Treasury yield
indicators.eli5: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years. When it rises, safe bonds compete with shares, and expensive stocks are the first to look less attractive.

indicators.label: Unemployment rate
indicators.detail: U-3 unemployment, October 2026, BLS via FRED
indicators.eli5: The share of people looking for work who cannot find it. Very low unemployment is where booms peak; once it starts rising, the economy is usually already turning.

indicators.label: Subprime auto loan delinquency
indicators.detail: Subprime auto 60+ day delinquency, Aug 2026, Trading Econ.
indicators.eli5: The share of riskier car loans more than two months behind on payments. Car loans go bad early when households are squeezed, so this is an early warning for the economy.

indicators.label: Chicago Fed financial conditions
indicators.detail: NFCI, negative means looser than average, FRED
indicators.eli5: The Chicago Fed's one-number summary of how easy money is: credit, borrowing and market stress. Below zero means easier than usual, the conditions bubbles grow in.

indicators.label: Semiconductor index ÷ S&P 500
indicators.detail: PHLX Semiconductor ÷ S&P 500 close, Yahoo chart data
indicators.eli5: The main chip-maker index compared with the S&P 500. Chips are the picks and shovels of the AI boom, so this shows how much of the market's bet is riding on it.

indicators.label: Hyperscaler capex ÷ cash flow
indicators.detail: MSFT+GOOGL+AMZN+META, Q2 2026, SEC XBRL 10-Q/10-K cash flows
indicators.eli5: What Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta spend on data centres and chips, as a share of the cash their businesses make. Near 100% means they spend about all they earn.

indicators.label: TSMC monthly revenue growth
indicators.detail: September 2026 revenue NT$511.86bn, TSMC press release
indicators.eli5: How fast sales are growing at TSMC, the company that makes nearly every advanced AI chip. Its order book is an early read on whether AI demand is still speeding up.

composite.reason: Hot CPI, rate-hike odds and the Nvidia CEO probe outweigh the chip rebound, so news adds +1.

fundamentals.label: S&P 500 forward 12-month P/E
fundamentals.note: equal to its 10-year average of 19.1 and below the 5-year 19.8 (FactSet)
fundamentals.eli5: Share prices divided by the profits analysts expect over the next year. At its ten-year average, prices are not running ahead of expected earnings.

fundamentals.label: S&P 500 Q3 earnings growth, est.
fundamentals.note: Q3 2026 estimate as of 9 October; forward P/E 19.1 (FactSet)
fundamentals.eli5: How much more profit the 500 biggest US companies are expected to have made this quarter than a year ago. Fast growth means real earnings, not just hope, back prices.

fundamentals.label: TSMC September revenue growth
fundamentals.eli5: How fast sales are growing at TSMC, the company that makes nearly every advanced AI chip. Its order book is an early read on whether AI demand is still speeding up.
